cor.heading: Revenue and Cost of Sales
cor.text:
For the three and nine months ended February 28, 2025, the Company generated total revenue of $7,500 and $22,500, respectively, from renting. The cost of sales for the three and nine months ended February 28, 2025, were $7,356 and $22,068, respectively.

For the three and nine months ended February 29, 2024, the Company generated total revenue of $7,500 and $22,500, respectively. The cost of sales for the three and nine months ended February 29, 2024, were $6,877 and $20,616, respectively.

The revenue and costs for both periods were almost the same reflecting the rent revenue and cost of sales that were aligned with the sublease.

opex.text:

The operating expenses for the three months ended February 28, 2025, included professional fees of $10,274; depreciation expense of $1,061 and general and administrative expenses of $55,597.

Total operating expenses for the three and nine months ended February 29, 2024, were $63,485 and $176,055, respectively. The operating expenses for the nine months ended February 29, 2024, included professional fees of $66,887; depreciation expense of $3,183 and general and administrative expenses of $105,985. The operating expenses for the three months ended February 29, 2024, included professional fees of $12,887; depreciation expense of $1,061 and general and administrative expenses of $49,537.

The increase in operating expenses is related to the increase of the rental expenses as more rental properties were leased by the Company in January and February of 2024.

nonop.heading: Other Income (Expense)
nonop.text:
The total other income (expense) for the three months ended February 28, 2025 and February 29, 2024 were $96,303 and $(5,113), respectively. The other expenses for the three months ended February 28, 2025, contained interest expense - related party of $15,943, and the gain of $112,246 on the amortization of debt premium, while for the three months ended February 29, 2024, the other expenses contained only interest expense - related party of $5,113. The significant increase in other income is due to the gain on the amortization of the debt premium.

The total other income (expense) for the nine months ended February 28, 2025 and February 29, 2024 were $(266,573) and $(13,348), respectively. The other expenses for the nine months ended February 28, 2025, contained interest expense - related party of $46,912, loss of $551,677 on the settlement of debt, gain of $332,016 on the amortization of debt premium, while for the nine months ended February 29, 2024, the other expenses contained only interest expense - related party of $13,348. The significant increase in other expenses is due to the loss on settlement of debt resulting from the convertible note paying for the unpaid rent, related party advances and unpaid interest owed to the related party.

net.heading: Net income (Loss)
net.text: The net income (loss) for the three months ended February 28, 2025 and February 29, 2024 was $29,515 and $(67,974), respectively. The net income (loss) for the nine months ended February 28, 2025 and February 29, 2024 was $(500,509) and $(187,528), respectively.

opex.text:
Total operating expenses for the three months ended August 31, 2026 were $42,384, consisting of professional fees of $14,000, depreciation expense of $1,061 and general and administrative expenses of $27,323.

Total operating expenses for the three months ended August 31, 2025 were $84,535, consisting of professional fees of $21,000, depreciation expense of $1,061 and general and administrative expenses of $62,474.

Total operating expenses decreased by $42,151, or 50%, compared with the prior-year quarter. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower general and administrative expenses, including lower occupancy costs following the expiration of the 2652 Blanding Boulevard lease in January 2026. Professional fees also decreased by $7,000, from $21,000 to $14,000, primarily because audit fees were $8,000 in the current-year quarter compared with $15,000 in

the prior-year quarter due to timing of audit fees incurred, while legal and accounting and consulting fees were unchanged.

net sales.heading: Rent Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company recognizes rent revenue from the lease of its sub-leased properties in accordance with ASC 842, Leases. The sub-lease is categorized as an operating lease according to ASC criteria for the lease definitions. Rent revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term, reflecting the pattern of the economic benefits derived from the lease.

The Company’s leases generally have fixed rental payments over the lease term, with occasional escalations based on predetermined factors. Rent revenue is recognized monthly as the lessor fulfills its obligations under the lease agreement.

Any lease incentives or concessions provided to lessees, such as rent-free periods or tenant improvement allowances, are recognized as a reduction of rent revenue over the lease term.

For the three months ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company recognized rental income of $21,000 (from a related party) and $0, respectively.

intro.text: Cannabis Suisse Corp. (“Company”) was incorporated in the State of Nevada on February 26, 2016. Since June 2022, the Company has focused on real estate operations and has had no involvement in any aspect of the cannabis industry. The Company leases commercial properties from entities controlled by its Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”). In March 2026, the Company entered into a sublease arrangement with a different entity controlled by its CEO for a portion of the property located at 10 N Newnan Street, Jacksonville, Florida. See Note 9.
